jobs.title: Director, Data & Technology
jobs.description:
Director, Data & Technology

Communitech helps tech companies start, grow, and succeed in Waterloo Region.

We’re building a tech ecosystem that’s proudly local, globally ambitious and powered by community.

Since 1997, Communitech has brought community and tech together to build Canada’s most vibrant innovation ecosystem. We connect local startups and scale-ups to the support they need to grow, compete and lead.

Today, that means helping trusted AI solutions reach the market, turning bold ideas into valuable IP, expanding peer and advisory networks for founders, and uniting voices through the Waterloo Tech Coalition to take on the issues that matter most.

Our goal is to keep Waterloo Region the most connected, collaborative, and resilient tech hub in the country.

We’re looking to grow our team with passionate people – people who believe in our mission and who are willing to do what it takes to help our founders succeed. If you like to work collaboratively, get s#!t done and be a champion for Canadian tech, we want to hear from you. Wonder what it’s like to work at Communitech? Learn more at https://www.communitech.ca/corporate-stuff/careers/.

Communitech is based in downtown Kitchener, Ontario. We work in-office five days a week because great things happen when we're together — creating space for deeper collaboration and stronger relationships with each other and the ecosystem we support.

Role Overview

We are seeking a strategic, forward-thinking, and hands-on leader to oversee Communitech’s Data and Technology functions. Reporting directly to the CFO, the Director of Data & Technology will oversee IT infrastructure, enterprise applications, cyber security, web operations, and data governance.

With our core technical foundation in place, this leader will bring the vision and hands-on expertise needed to transform Communitech’s data assets into actionable strategy, champion responsible AI adoption to streamline internal workflows, and maintain resilient, high-performing IT operations for our staff, facility tenants, and the broader Waterloo Region tech ecosystem.

Key Responsibilities

AI Innovation & Workflow Integration
Lead the identification, evaluation, and adoption of modern AI tools (generative AI, automation scripts, LLM integrations) across internal teams to optimize operations and reduce administrative friction.
Establish clear guidelines, privacy standards, and ethical guardrails for data security and safe AI usage across the organization.
Stay ahead of emerging technology trends to ensure Communitech’s tech stack reflects best practices, positioning our non-profit as a forward-thinking leader in the AI-driven tech landscape.

Strategic Data & Analytics Leadership
Foster a culture of storytelling with data across the organization.
Enable decision making and ensure ecosystem trends, member needs, and non-profit reporting metrics are continuously illuminated through actionable reporting and business intelligence solutions.
Oversee the modernization and integrity of Communitech’s data and analytics infrastructure to maintain data integrity, security, and scalability.

Enterprise IT, Infrastructure, and Web Operations
Lead internal teams and external partners across IT operations, cloud platforms, web development, and application management to deliver high availability and exceptional service quality for our teams and on-site hub tenants.
Act as the primary authority on organizational cyber risk, developing, executing, and monitoring risk mitigation strategies, compliance protocols, and incident response frameworks to protect member and organizational data.

Team Leadership & Operations
Lead, coach and develop high-performing Data and Technology teams.
Maintain a strong track record of completing technical and operational projects on time and within budget through modern project management methodologies and AI-assisted workflows.
Partner closely with internal leaders to align technology roadmaps with overall business objectives and ecosystem needs.
Foster a culture of responsiveness, ownership, collaboration and continuous improvement.

What Success Looks Like

The Director, Data & Technology will make Communitech more valuable, relevant, and indispensable to the members and community we serve.

Success in this role will include:
Successfully introducing AI-driven tooling and automation that noticeably reduces manual overhead across programs, reporting, and internal operations.
Delivering clean, real-time dashboards and impact analytics that clearly measure member engagement and ecosystem health for various stakeholders.
Maintaining an exceptionally reliable, secure, and modern IT environment for the Communitech team and hub facility tenants.
Establish a resilient security posture that protects sensitive startup and organizational data against evolving threats.
Foster an empowered, agile team culture grounded in ownership, responsiveness, continuous learning, and continuous improvement.

Qualifications

5+ years of progressive technology leadership experience across enterprise IT, data engineering, software development, or digital transformation (non-profit or innovation hub experience is a strong asset).
Hands-on understanding of how to practically integrate modern AI tools, automation, and SaaS platforms into workplace processes to maximize non-profit efficiency.
Broad technical grasp across Web, Security, and IT with expertise in data architecture, Business Intelligence, and advanced reporting solutions.
Proven ability to manage, inspire, and develop multi-disciplinary technical teams while remaining willing to dive deep into execution when necessary
Technical Breadth:
Solid architecture understanding of cloud data stacks and web platforms
Deep understanding of networking fundamentals, SaaS platforms, and enterprise cyber security best practices.
Strong track record managing technology vendors, external service providers, and outsourced partners.
Strong business acumen and project management discipline with a history of delivering operational and technical projects on time and within budget.
A strong, member-centric mindset with a deep passion for supporting entrepreneurs, tech start ups, and the local innovation ecosystem.

Compensation

The annual base salary range is $100,000-$115,000. The actual compensation will be based on various factors, including the candidate’s level of skills, experience and education.

To Apply

Please apply online along with your resume and cover letter.

We thank all applicants in advance; however only individuals selected for an interview will be contacted. All applications will be kept confidential. Communitech is a diverse and inclusive environment and encourages applications from all qualified candidates, including aboriginal persons, francophones, members of sexual minority groups, persons with disabilities, visible minorities, and women. We will provide any requested accommodation to candidates with disabilities throughout the recruitment process.

In compliance with Ontario’s Bill 190, we confirm that this posting represents a current, existing vacancy within our organization.

ADP’s platform uses AI to generate Profile Relevance scores. All applications will be reviewed by a human. Scores do not affect the visibility of an application and applicants may opt-out when applying.

jobs.title: Senior Director, Analytics and Data Science, Core Product & Growth
jobs.description:
About Life360

Life360's mission is to keep people close to the ones they love. Our category-leading mobile app, Tile tracking devices, and Pet GPS tracker empower members to protect the people, pets, and things they care about most with a range of services, including location sharing, safe driver reports, and crash detection with emergency dispatch. Life360 serves approximately 102.4 million monthly active users (MAU), as of June 30, 2026, across more than 180 countries.

Life360 delivers peace of mind and enhances everyday family life with seamless coordination for all the moments that matter, big and small. By continuing to innovate and deliver for our customers, we have become a household name and the must-have mobile-based membership for families (and those friends who are basically family).

Life360 has more than 500 (and growing!) remote-first employees. For more information, please visit life360.com.

Life360 is a Remote First company, which means a remote work environment will be the primary experience for all employees. All positions, unless otherwise specified, can be performed remotely (within the US and Canada) regardless of any specified location above.

We are AI Native

We are building an AI native company where AI is an integral part of how we build and operate. AI tool usage during interviews varies by role. You may be asked to demonstrate proficiency with AI tools, discuss how you leverage AI, or complete interview exercises without AI assistance. Your Recruiter will provide clear guidance as you move through the interview process.

Undisclosed use of AI not previously discussed with or approved by your Recruiter may impact your candidacy.

About The Team

The Data & Analytics Team (DnA) is a 60+ person organization spanning data engineering, analytics engineering, analytics/decision science, and data science/ML. The science teams are organized into two sub teams, focusing on MAU and Revenue. This role leads decision science and data science within MAU.

You and your team will be responsible for understanding the drivers behind MAU: why members come, why they stay, and why they return. The team partners with product, marketing, and engineering to put those learnings into everyday work, and that work shapes our roadmaps.

Our data is unusual for a consumer company. Life360 measures families and circles rather than individuals, so one member's behavior affects another's, which makes measurement a different problem than a standard funnel. With billions of location events, driving behavior, crash detection, and Tile and Pet GPS trackers, we get a rich picture of physical behavior that few consumer companies can build.

About The Job

This Senior Director leads MAU Analytics and Data Science.

You and your team will work across acquisition, activation, engagement, and retention on the analysis, models, and experiments behind each. A lot of what this role owns needs to be built rather than maintained: the measurement, the standards, and how the team uses AI. The team is also raising its craft, and coaching people through that is an important part of the job. Within a year, your team members will be operating at an elevated skill level, proactively bringing key questions to light, and serving as trusted advisors whom stakeholders consult for strategic guidance rather than simple task execution.

You will report to the Head of Data and work closely with counterparts leading Revenue Analytics and Data Science, and with the leaders of Data Engineering.

For candidates based in the US, the salary range for this position is $247,000 to $366,000 USD. For candidates based out of Canada, the salary range for this position is $286,000 to $339,000 CAD.
We take into consideration an individual's background, job-related knowledge, skills, and experience in determining final salary. Base pay may also vary based on geographic location, with US work locations falling into one of three geographic tiers.

Total compensation is inclusive of equity compensation in the form of Restricted Stock Units (RSUs)
, as well as a comprehensive benefits package, including medical, dental, vision, financial, and other benefits.

What You'll Do

Lead and develop the decision scientists and data scientists on the team, and set the quality bar for both disciplines.
Own the MAU driver model and the forecast.
Own the exploratory work that drives the strategy to grow MAU.
Establish how an analysis gets scoped, run, reviewed, and written up, so its quality does not depend on who picked up the request.
Partner with your Revenue counterpart and Data Engineering leadership to define common metrics, align on experimentation standards, and introduce unified operating practices across teams.
Build the operating model that gets the team into the roadmap conversation early, with a view on what to build and what to test.
Use agents and automated analysis daily, and expect the same of the team.
Shape how the team works AI-native: what gets delegated to agents, what gets automated, and what stays human judgment.

What We're Looking For

Required Experience & Qualifications

10+ years in analytics, data science, or decision science, including 5+ years in people management in a senior leadership role.
Deep expertise in inferential and causal analytics. Able to lead ML practitioners.
Expert knowledge of engagement, retention, churn, and cohort metrics.
Experience forecasting a company-level metric and being held to it.
SQL, plus Python or R.
Experience with Databricks, third party experimentation tools (e.g. Statsig), Tableau or similar BI tools, and AI native BI tools (e.g. Hex, AI/BI).
Hands-on with coding agents (Claude Code or equivalent) in your own analytical work.
Bachelor's degree or equivalent.

Nice to Have

Familiarity with experiment design to identify and control for network effects.
Master’s degree or PhD with an emphasis in social science, psychology or other behavioral science.
Experience leading a team that reports to you but sits embedded with product and engineering teams.
Experience in a B2C subscription business.

Core Expectations

You have moved an analytics team from reactive to embedded.
You coach and develop people, and you have grown analysts into leaders.
On your teams, analysis starts from a hypothesis rather than a data request.
You have built the standards a team works from, and got people to use them.
You are curious about why people behave the way they do, not just what they did.
You decide what the team does not work on, and you can defend it.

Our Benefits

Medical, dental, vision, life and disability insurance plans (100% paid for US employees). We offer life and disability as well as supplemental plans for medical and dental for Canadian employees.
401(k) plan with company matching program in the US and RRSP with DPSP plan for Canadian employees.
Paid parental leave
Mental Wellness Program & Employee Assistance Program (EAP) for mental well-being
Generous time off: flexible PTO, companywide holidays throughout the year plus summer and winter shutdowns
Learning & Development programs
Equipment, tools, and reimbursement support for a productive remote environment.
Free Life360 Platinum Membership and Tile trackers.

Life360 Values

Our company's mission-driven culture is guided by our shared values to create a trusted work environment where you can bring your authentic self to work and make a positive difference

Be a Good Person - We have a team of high integrity people you can trust.
Be Direct With Respect - We communicate directly, even when it's hard.
Members Before Metrics - We focus on building an exceptional experience for families.
High Intensity, High Impact - We do whatever it takes to get the job done.

Our Commitment to Diversity

We believe that different ideas, perspectives and backgrounds create a stronger and more creative work environment that delivers better results. Together, we continue to build an inclusive culture that encourages, supports, and celebrates the diverse voices of our employees. It fuels our innovation and connects us closer to our customers and the communities we serve. We strive to create a workplace that reflects the communities we serve and where everyone feels empowered to bring their authentic best selves to work.

We are an equal opportunity employer and value diversity at Life360. We do not discriminate on the basis of race, religion, color, national origin, gender, sexual orientation, age, marital status, veteran status, disability status or any legally protected status.

We encourage people of all backgrounds to apply. We believe that a diversity of perspectives and experiences create a foundation for the best ideas. Come join us in building something meaningful. Even if you don't meet 100% of the below qualifications, you should still seriously consider applying!

jobs.title: Director of Finance
jobs.location: St John’s, Newfoundland and Labrador, Canada
jobs.description:
Higher Talent
is excited to conduct an executive search for a strategic, hands-on, entrepreneurial Director of Finance
for Fort Amherst Healthcare,
in St. John’s, NL.

WHO WE ARE
:

Fort Amherst Healthcare, a subsidiary of Fort Amherst Properties, is an investment company headquartered in St. John’s focused on the development of high-quality seniors housing and health care services. The company currently owns and operates approximately 400 personal care home suites across the province, consisting of both licensed personal care homes and independent living seniors' apartments. Facilities under management include Bishops Gardens (St John’s), Westbury Estates (Southlands), Mountain View Retirement Centre (Corner Brook), Cambridge Estates (St. John’s).

With happiness, health and wellness as top priorities, we strive to offer an extensive range of services, living options, and lifestyle choices to meet individual needs - whether highly active, needing a little assistance day-to-day, or requiring a custom-designed care plan.

To learn more about us, please visit Fort Amherst Healthcare.

THE ROLE:

The Director of Finance is a strategic, hands-on finance leader with a strong accounting foundation and demonstrated experience managing the financial operations of a complex, people-focused organization. The successful candidate will build and professionalize the finance function, establish scalable corporate systems and partner closely with the President, Director of Operations, site leadership, the Board, lenders and external advisors.

RESPONSIBILITIES:

Reporting to the President, the Director of Finance will lead accounting, financial reporting, planning and analysis, treasury, banking, tax, audit coordination, lender and Board reporting and financial controls. The role will also oversee defined corporate-support functions including information technology, insurance, contracting, procurement, supply-chain governance, vendor administration and shared-service coordination.

Financial Leadership & Reporting

Lead accounting and financial reporting across all properties and legal entities.
Own monthly close, budgeting, forecasting, cash flow, financial controls and scenario analysis.
Standardize accounting practices, policies, controls and reporting processes.
Translate financial results, risks and opportunities into actionable recommendations for the President and Board.

Treasury, Tax & Risk

Oversee cash management, banking, treasury, tax, audit coordination and lender reporting.
Support financing, lender diligence, covenant compliance and transaction requirements.
Oversee insurance, risk management and related regulatory requirements.

Systems & Business Operations

Modernize financial systems, reporting and workflow automation.
Oversee technology infrastructure, cybersecurity, continuity and third-party providers.
Establish scalable processes for contracts, procurement, vendors and shared services

Systems & Business Operations

Modernize financial systems, reporting and workflow automation.
Oversee technology infrastructure, cybersecurity, continuity and third-party providers.
Establish scalable processes for contracts, procurement, vendors and shared services.

Growth & Integration

Support M&A diligence, financing and transaction execution.
Lead finance, banking, insurance, systems and vendor integration for acquisitions and new entities.
Build scalable shared-service processes as the organization grows.

Leadership & Partnership

Serve as a trusted financial and business advisor to the President.
Partner closely with the Director of Operations and site leadership.
Strengthen financial understanding and accountability across the organization.
Lead and develop finance and business-support personnel as the function grows.

ABOUT YOU:

CPA designation.
7+ years of progressive financial leadership experience; experience in healthcare, long-term care, seniors living, or another regulated, multi-site environment is an asset.
Degree or diploma in Accounting, Finance, Business Administration, or a related discipline.
Strong experience in budgeting, forecasting, financial reporting, cash flow management, and financial controls.
Strong business acumen with the ability to connect financial performance to operational realities.
Exceptional analytical, organizational, and problem-solving skills with strong attention to detail.
Proven leadership experience with the ability to mentor, develop, and motivate a team.
Experience with accounting/ERP systems and advanced Microsoft Excel skills.
Proactive, hands-on approach with the ability to thrive in a fast-paced, evolving environment.
Knowledge of government funding programs and regulatory requirements is an asset.

WHAT YOU CAN EXPECT:

An attractive total compensation package, including a competitive salary, comprehensive benefits package, employer matched RRSP, personal time off, professional development and growth opportunities.

HOW TO APPLY:

If you are financially rigorous, commercially minded, and comfortable moving seamlessly between detailed execution and executive-level decision-making, this is an opportunity to make a meaningful impact. Bring your sound financial judgment, integrity, accountability, and leadership to Fort Amherst Healthcare—and take the next step in your career.

To apply in confidence online: Apply Here!

For more information, please contact:

Brendan Hagerty
| VP & General Manager | Brendan@highertalent.ca

and/or

Sarah French
| Senior Recruiter and HR Consultant | Sarah@highertalent.ca

At Higher Talent we recognize the value of diversity and are committed to making intentional steps toward building inclusive teams that better reflect the communities Higher Talent and the organizations we serve operate within. We believe that inclusion is not just about making room at the table but about seeking out talent through a diversity lens and letting everyone know that their unique perspectives are important contributions to building stronger workplaces in a changing world. We encourage all qualified candidates to apply for our posted positions. We welcome candidates to self-identify or make our recruitment team aware of any potential accommodations they may need during the recruitment process. This opportunity is only available for candidates legally entitled to work in Canada. We thank all applicants for their interest, however, only those candidates being considered for an interview will be contacted.

jobs.title: Disaster Recovery and Technology Resilience Leader, Deloitte Global Technology
jobs.description:
Job Type:
Permanent Work Model:
Remote Reference code:
133961 Primary Location:
Toronto, ON All Available Locations:
Toronto, ON; Ottawa, ON

Our Purpose

At Deloitte, our Purpose is to make an impact that matters. We exist to inspire and help our people, organizations, communities, and countries to thrive by building a better future. Our work underpins a prosperous society where people can find meaning and opportunity. It builds consumer and business confidence, empowers organizations to find imaginative ways of deploying capital, enables fair, trusted, and functioning social and economic institutions, and allows our friends, families, and communities to enjoy the quality of life that comes with a sustainable future. And as the largest 100% Canadian-owned and operated professional services firm in our country, we are proud to work alongside our clients to make a positive impact for all Canadians.

By living our Purpose, we will make an impact that matters.

Have many careers in one Firm.
Enjoy flexible, proactive, and practical benefits that foster a culture of well-being and connectedness.
Learn from deep subject matter experts through mentoring and on the job coaching

Deloitte Global is the engine of the Deloitte network. Our professionals reach across disciplines and borders to develop and lead global initiatives. We deliver strategic programs and services that unite our organization.

Work you'll do

The Deloitte Technology Disaster Recovery and Technology Resilience Leader is responsible for establishing, leading, and continuously maturing the technology resiliency framework across Deloitte Technology. Reporting to the Director of Process Optimization and Service Assurance, this role drives the enterprise-wide strategy for IT disaster recovery, in alignment with business continuity and operational resilience to ensure critical technology services remain available, recoverable, and aligned to business priorities. The individual partners closely with technology leaders, architects, engineers, analysts, and cross-functional stakeholders (Global Security Office, Technology Risk Office, member firm BC/DR Leaders) to develop, socialize, and validate comprehensive recovery and resiliency plans through regular testing, governance, and continuous improvement. This leader will design, implement, and integrate recovery & resiliency processes, programs, and procedures using industry best practices and recognized frameworks such as ITIL, COBIT, PMBOK, and CMMI.

What will your typical day look like?

Job Responsibilities:

Develop, implement, and lead a comprehensive Technology Disaster Recovery & Resiliency practice within DT, including governance, standards, planning, testing, reporting, and continuous improvement.
Partner with competency area leads and key stakeholders to identify action owners, define accountabilities, and ensure timely execution, testing, and adherence to IT disaster recovery & resiliency plans.
Design, enhance, and maintain resiliency processes, standards, and controls to protect, sustain, and recover hardware and software operations throughout the full technology lifecycle.
Lead the design, coordination, and execution of Disaster Recovery (DR) capabilities across service & product teams and related, supporting functions.
Collaborate with technology and business leaders to define the resiliency roadmap, strategy, objectives, key performance indicators, and success metrics for BCP, DR, and broader technology resilience initiatives.
Monitor and evaluate the execution and effectiveness of resiliency plans, including periodic exercises, functional recovery testing, tabletop simulations, and remediation of identified gaps.
Ensure alignment of resiliency strategies with the overall information technology strategy, enterprise risk posture, security requirements, and other IT service management processes.
Own and maintain all relevant process documentation, implementation guidance, operating procedures, testing evidence, metrics, and leadership reporting related to technology resiliency.
Produce and deliver key outputs including resiliency strategies, recovery plans, testing schedules, executive dashboards, metrics, and risk or audit reports.
Partner with Controls and Assurance teams to integrate resiliency requirements into audit readiness activities, ensure testing evidence is current, and support internal and external audits through issue tracking and remediation oversight.
Manage the cost, risk, performance, and service quality attributes associated with resiliency-related programs, tools, and capabilities.
Lead, coach, and develop direct reports by fostering a high-performance environment centered on client service, teamwork, accountability, recognition, and mutual respect.
Support employee development through goal setting, performance feedback, succession planning, and training oversight to ensure completion of required departmental and company learning programs.

About The Team

Deloitte Technology works at the forefront of technology development and processes to support and protect Deloitte around the world. In this truly global environment, we operate not in "what is" but rather "what can be" to help Deloitte deliver and connect with its clients, its communities, and one another in ways not previously conceived.

Qualifications

Enough about us, let’s talk about you

Bachelor’s degree in Information Technology, Computer Science, Business, Management, or a related field required
Minimum of 7 years of experience in a complex business and information systems environment.
At least 4 years of experience in a managerial or senior managerial leadership capacity.
Minimum of 5 years of experience in IT Business Continuity Planning, Disaster Recovery, and Technology Resilience.
Demonstrated expertise in IT support processes, operational controls, and service management functions.
Strong understanding of industry frameworks and best practices such as ITIL, COBIT, PMBOK, and CMMI.
Experience leading cross-functional programs, influencing senior stakeholders, and driving enterprise-wide resiliency initiatives.

Preferred Qualifications:

Master’s degree in Information Technology, Computer Science, Business, Management or related field.
ITIL v3 or v4 certification is not required but is strongly preferred.
Experience with ServiceNow ITSM or similar service management platforms is a plus.

Total Rewards

The salary range for this position is $104,000 - $215,000, and individuals may be eligible to participate in our bonus program. Deloitte is fair and competitive when it comes to the salaries of our people. We regularly benchmark across a variety of positions, industries, sectors, targets, and levels. Our approach is grounded on recognizing people's unique strengths and contributions and rewarding the value that they deliver.

Our Total Rewards Package extends well beyond traditional compensation and benefit programs and is designed to recognize employee contributions, encourage personal wellness, and support firm growth. Along with a competitive base salary and variable pay opportunities, we offer a wide array of initiatives that differentiate us as a people-first organization. On top of our regular paid vacation days, some examples include: $4,000 per year for mental health support benefits, a $1,300 flexible benefit spending account, firm-wide closures known as "Deloitte Days", dedicated days of for learning (known as Development and Innovation Days), flexible work arrangements and a hybrid work structure.

Our promise to our people: Deloitte is where potential comes to life.

Be yourself, and more.

We are a group of talented people who want to learn, gain experience, and develop skills. Wherever you are in your career, we want you to advance.

You Shape How We Make Impact.

Diverse perspectives and life experiences make us better. Whoever you are and wherever you’re from, we want you to feel like you belong here. We provide flexible working options to support you and how you can contribute.

Be the leader you want to be

Some guide teams, some change culture, some build essential expertise. We offer opportunities and experiences that support your continuing growth as a leader.

Have as many careers as you want.

We are uniquely able to offer you new challenges and roles – and prepare you for them. We bring together people with unique experiences and talents, and we are the place to develop a lasting network of friends, peers, and mentors.

The next step is yours

At Deloitte, we are all about doing business inclusively – that starts with having diverse colleagues of all abilities. Deloitte encourages applications from all qualified candidates who represent the full diversity of communities across Canada. This includes, but is not limited to, people with disabilities, candidates from Indigenous communities, and candidates from the Black community in support of living our values, creating a culture of Diversity Equity and Inclusion and our commitment to our AccessAbility Action Plan, Reconciliation Action Plan and the BlackNorth Initiative.

We encourage you to connect with us at accessiblecareers@deloitte.ca if you require an accommodation for the recruitment process (including alternate formats of materials, accessible meeting rooms or other accommodations) or indigenouscareers@deloitte.ca for any questions relating to careers for Indigenous peoples at Deloitte (First Nations, Inuit, Métis).

When you apply, we will review your application using Deloitte's Global Talent Standards to ensure a consistent recruitment experience. Our recruitment advisors and hiring teams will utilize human screening combined with AI technology to help identify the skills and qualities that matter most to our business, while safeguarding your privacy and using AI responsibly.

Deloitte Canada has 20 offices with representation across most of the country. We acknowledge that Deloitte offices stand on traditional, treaty, and unceded territories in what is now known as Canada. We recognize that Indigenous Peoples have been the caretakers of this land since time immemorial, nurturing its resources and preserving its natural beauty. We acknowledge this land is still home to many First Nations, Inuit, and Métis Peoples, who continue to maintain their deep connection to the land and its sacred teachings. We humbly acknowledge that we are all Treaty people, and we commit to fostering a relationship of respect, collaboration, and stewardship with Indigenous communities in our shared goal of reconciliation and environmental sustainability.

Qualifications

Enough about us, let’s talk about you

Bachelor’s degree in Information Technology, Computer Science, Business, Management, or a related field required
Minimum of 7 years of experience in a complex business and information systems environment.
At least 4 years of experience in a managerial or senior managerial leadership capacity.
Minimum of 5 years of experience in IT Business Continuity Planning, Disaster Recovery, and Technology Resilience.
Demonstrated expertise in IT support processes, operational controls, and service management functions.
Strong understanding of industry frameworks and best practices such as ITIL, COBIT, PMBOK, and CMMI.
Experience leading cross-functional programs, influencing senior stakeholders, and driving enterprise-wide resiliency initiatives.

Preferred Qualifications:

Master’s degree in Information Technology, Computer Science, Business, Management or related field.
ITIL v3 or v4 certification is not required but is strongly preferred.
Experience with ServiceNow ITSM or similar service management platforms is a plus.

Total Rewards

The salary range for this position is $104,000 - $215,000, and individuals may be eligible to participate in our bonus program. Deloitte is fair and competitive when it comes to the salaries of our people. We regularly benchmark across a variety of positions, industries, sectors, targets, and levels. Our approach is grounded on recognizing people's unique strengths and contributions and rewarding the value that they deliver.

Our Total Rewards Package extends well beyond traditional compensation and benefit programs and is designed to recognize employee contributions, encourage personal wellness, and support firm growth. Along with a competitive base salary and variable pay opportunities, we offer a wide array of initiatives that differentiate us as a people-first organization. On top of our regular paid vacation days, some examples include: $4,000 per year for mental health support benefits, a $1,300 flexible benefit spending account, firm-wide closures known as "Deloitte Days", dedicated days of for learning (known as Development and Innovation Days), flexible work arrangements and a hybrid work structure.
